faq.question: What is Palermo Soho known for food-wise?
faq.answer: Palermo Soho is Buenos Aires' trendiest dining neighborhood with world-class parrillas, chef-driven restaurants, and Asian fusion. Home to Don Julio (#8 worldwide) and El Preferido.

faq.question: How much does dinner cost?
faq.answer: $15–$35 USD mid-range. Budget spots $12–$20. Fine dining $30–$60. Argentina's exchange rate makes top restaurants affordable.

faq.question: Do I need reservations?
faq.answer: For Don Julio, El Preferido, Anchoíta — yes. Mid-range spots are fine for walk-ins on weekdays.

faq.question: What time is dinner?
faq.answer: 9 PM – midnight for locals. Restaurants open 7-8 PM. Arriving at 8 PM avoids waits.

faq.question: Is it safe at night?
faq.answer: Yes — one of BA's safest neighborhoods for tourists. Lively until past midnight.

faq.question: Soho vs Hollywood?
faq.answer: Soho has big-name restaurants. Hollywood has more nightlife. 10-minute walk apart.

methodology: We analyzed 150+ Reddit posts and 800+ comments across r/BuenosAires, r/finedining, r/travel, and r/chubbytravel — spanning 2022 to 2026. Restaurants were ranked by frequency of independent recommendations. Every venue was enriched with Google Places API data (ratings, hours, addresses) and cross-referenced with food blogs including Eater, Condé Nast Traveler, and TimeOut Buenos Aires.
